headline: Hidden SHA-256 DNA checks pin the compressed byte counts of one specific LZW table-full/CLEAR-timing policy the instruction never states; 4 of 14 rollouts shipped fully valid BigTIFFs that imagecodecs 2024.9.22 decodes bit-exactly — including the exact policy imagecodecs' own LZW encoder uses — and still scored 0.0.

One hardcoded assertion (unique_valueset_oid_count == 97) encodes a reference-implementation bug — counting a comma-joined <allowedValuesetOids> text node as a single OID — and zeroes 13 otherwise-complete solutions under all-or-nothing grading; 15/15 rollouts computed 96.

All 14 rollouts diagnosed and fixed all five stated bugs; pass/fail is decided entirely by which of several equally-valid Dagster spellings the agent picked (run_coordinator vs run_queue in dagster.yaml, unconditional context.run_id vs upstream_output inside _get_path, run_key vs cursor dedup) — none of which the instruction states or the container reveals.

Tests hard-code the reference implementation's private JSON item schema (region1/region2, end, type, unpadded hex()) that the instruction never states; a 2-line logic-free rename drops the reference from 27/27 to 0.0, and all 15 rollouts made exactly such a rename.

The graph_stats cross-check resolves "the union FST" by grabbing the first /app/fsts entry whose name merely contains "union", so a solver that obeys the instruction to put intermediate FSTs there under descriptive names (union_abc.fst, ...) gets an arbitrary partial automaton dotted and fails despite byte-identical, fully correct deliverables.
A hidden `--help` must-exit-0 assertion, absent from the instruction and from every file in the container, zeroes 12 of 13 otherwise-complete solutions under all-or-nothing scoring.

Verifier demands a factually wrong `usart2`->`uart2` rename (a regression Renode itself reversed in v1.13.0 and upstream reversed in 2022) that blocks 15/15 rollouts, plus an unstated 64K RAM constant contradicting the RM0090 reference the instruction cites.

All 15 rollouts completed every objectively-checkable remediation, then were zeroed by 28 exact-match assertions on a subjective status/severity table that the shipped rubric does not determine and the reference solution simply hardcodes.

Verifier's five-name wrapper whitelist bans `loop-mssa` — the only legal nesting for `licm`, which available_passes.txt advertises — and its `\b`-anchored remove/swap regexes corrupt `aggressive-instcombine`; together these zeroed 14/15 rollouts that met every stated constraint.
Rollouts are not isolated: concurrent runs share one OpenBao on 127.0.0.1:8200, and r14 deleted+recreated app-data out from under r13's finished, correct work, turning it into a 0.0.

The sole failing rollout put `#include <time.h>` in src/timing.h instead of src/timing.c — a functionally identical fix that produced a clean build and a correct .deb — but the verifier text-greps /app/src/timing.c specifically, so an otherwise complete solution scored 0.0.

One hidden assertion pins the anomalies-array emission order (out-of-order before checksum for staging V5); the instruction lists the rules in the opposite order, so six spec-faithful, fully-correct implementations score 0.0 and the two passers differ only by array position.

The task is well-specified and strongly graded in 14/15 containers, but r01 was provisioned with a stale image whose /app/affine_toolkit.py had no register_affine_landmarks/chain_resample stubs and whose SPEC.md (109 lines vs 158) documented neither function, making the API the verifier pins undiscoverable — its correct five-bug fix scored 0.

All 15 rollouts delivered an equivalent compliant end state, but r01's container was provisioned without tasks/validate.yml — the only place the module parameter names the verifier greps for are written — and r14 was zeroed for naming its entrypoint run_module() instead of main(); both zeros measure module-interface trivia, not the hardening work.

The verifier's hard gate is a full `ansible-playbook` run whose very first task is `apt: update_cache: yes` — and `apt-get update` cannot succeed in this sandbox fleet, so no solver (not even the shipped reference) can score above 0, while 13/15 rollouts delivered the exact oracle diff.

Following the instruction's own mandated step (`pip install schemathesis`) installs pytest 9 plus a pytest11 plugin importing `_pytest.subtests`; tests/test.sh then force-downgrades pytest to 8.3.4, so `python3 -m pytest` crashes at plugin autoload with exit 1 before collecting a single test — reward 0.0 regardless of the repair.

All four zero-reward rollouts wrote artifacts that pass all 16 assertions; their containers had JPL egress killed at the TLS layer, and the verifier's own module-scoped fixture makes a live GET to that same unreachable host, so a perfect solution (including the reference) scores 0.0 there.

The head.csv baked into the shipped image is far noisier than the data the verifier was calibrated against, so the hidden `assert evp > 80.0` is unreachable by any of the three prescribed models (all cap at 71.09%) — the packaged reference solution itself would fail, and 12 of 15 rollouts were zeroed on that single assertion despite recovering the documented ground-truth parameters.

tests/test_state.py imports the reference implementation from /solution at module scope, a path absent from the verification container, so pytest errors during collection (exit 2) and every rollout — including 14 that produced byte-exact reference results and a valid 192/1584 DOT — is scored 0.0.

Concurrent rollout containers share a PID/network namespace, so only one container's postgres can bind :5432 — losers silently do all their DDL inside a co-tenant's database and are scored 0 (r05, r07) while their own app_db stays pre-migration; the reference solve.sh would fail identically.

The v2 environment is clean and correctly graded for 14 rollouts, but r01 ran against a stale v1 container image (spec.md/format.md/Go reference/buggy compiler all predate autogrouping, state conflicts and removed/purged states) while being graded by the v2 verifier, so its 0.0 was unattainable-by-design rather than earned.

r01 was handed a stale container whose /app/avl.py stops at `is_in` and contains none of the split/join/set-operation layer the verifier imports, so its 0.0 was unattainable-by-construction; the other 14 passes are fully earned, though the balance half of the grade is evaluated by the solver's own avl()/is_ord().

r01's container was built from an older image that lacks /app/challenge/audit_format.json — the only in-container source of the exact enum vocabulary the verifier demands — so a run that did the complete cryptanalysis and derived both flags scored 0.0 for using labels it had no way to learn.

The sole failing rollout (r01) ran against a stale container image whose /app/pipeline.py was a different 116-line file with no Stage 6/7 spec comments and none of the 7 bandpass/census result keys the verifier hard-requires, making its 0.0 an environment-induced false negative; separately, the verifier grades only the solver-written results.json, so a fabricated constants file would also score 1.0 (latent, unexercised).

r01 was graded against a /data/notes.txt it never had: its container shipped the pre-rebuild 2223-byte notes (Jun 13 10:54) that specifies plain CpG overlap and non-stranded TF counting, while the verifier enforces the >=50%-of-island and same-strand rules added in the 2455-byte revision (Jun 13 11:12) that all 14 passing rollouts received.

r01 was served a stale container image whose /app/schema.json (28 lines, 4 sections) and /app/properties.json (P1-P7) omit the vbs_ert / algorithm_selection / performance_profile sections that the verifier demands and that the instruction never names, so a fully correct solve scored 0.0 on section naming alone.

All four zero-reward rollouts delivered code that is semantically identical (in places diff-identical modulo comments) to the eleven that scored 1.0, and the four failures cluster perfectly on a single rollout date (2026-06-28), so the zeros track the grading batch, not the work.

tests/test.sh generates its ground truth by running /solution/backtest_fixed.py, but the grader uploads only tests/ to /tests and never creates /solution, so /tmp/reference_results.json is always missing and pytest exits 1 (reward 0.0) even for a byte-perfect solve — all 15 rollouts produced the exact reference numbers and all scored 0.

The one zero-reward rollout ran against a stale build of the unversioned docker tag whose /app/spec.md and /app/pipeline.sh describe only strict/lenient (zero mentions of "weighted" or "error_analysis" anywhere in its transcript), so the v2 verifier's weighted-mode and error-analysis assertions were unattainable in that container; the other 14 rollouts, on the correct image, all earned genuine 1.0s.

The single failing rollout ran against an older image whose /app/spec.md omitted the effect-size and bootstrap sections entirely — its numbers were all correct, including the bootstrap frequencies, and it failed only on schema keys its spec never documented.

Run r01 was launched against a stale container image whose /app/spec.md and /app/pipeline.py describe only FOUR sections (no RRF consensus, no activity_cliffs), while the fixed verifier requires five — making reward 0 unattainable for it no matter how good the solve; separately, a third of the graded work (virtual_screening) is never numerically checked.

The task as shipped is well specified and correctly graded (11 earned passes on an unbluffable SHA256 gate), but r01 ran against a stale container image whose audit_brief.txt lacked the recommended_fix schema and the entire generate_secure_keypairs API spec the verifier demands, so its 0.0 was unearnable.

The container ships no zarr, so every solver's `pip install zarr` yields 3.2.1 and writes a Zarr v3 store that the verifier's pinned zarr 2.18.2 physically cannot open — I reproduced it: the reference pipeline scores 31/31 when the writer is zarr 2.18.2 and 9/31 (reward 0.0) when it is zarr 3.2.1, with byte-identical results.json.

Two different /app/spec.md files were mounted across rollouts of the same task: r01's copy explicitly said the clang_parse JSON schema was "your design decision", the other 14 contained a "### JSON AST Schema" section pinning type/name/body/activations/target — and the verifier hardcodes those exact keys, so r01's byte-perfect solution scored 0.0 for using the freedom its own spec granted.

All 15 rollouts produced the same correct 5-finding miniframe query pack; the 11 that scored 0 differ only in that the CodeQL package registry happened to be reachable during their episode, so their documented `codeql pack install` pinned a HOME-local pack cache the verifier's independent re-run cannot resolve.

The grader's assembly parser cannot recognize any Clang function label, so its ground truth for "clang vectorizes kernel_optimized" is hardwired False and every honest solver that reports the true value fails the all-or-nothing suite.

The one failing rollout (r01) was served a stale /app/schema.json naming the fill_multiples boolean `has_add_induction_variable` while tests/test_state.py:202 reads `has_compiler_introduced_add`, so obeying the instruction ("answer every field defined in /app/schema.json") guaranteed a KeyError and, under all-or-nothing reward, zeroed otherwise-perfect work.

In 4 of 15 container instantiations the OSTk data cache the task text guarantees is "pre-populated" contained only manifest.json and the Git-LFS host serving the missing kernels was blocked, so `import ostk.astrodynamics` — and therefore tests/test_state.py:14-19 and the packet's own reference solution — crashed at collection (test_exit=2), zeroing three runs whose numbers were in fact correct to ~1e-8 km.

The single failing rollout (r01) was run against a stale v1 container image whose types.py has no Leaf/Container, whose DB has no compose_cases, and whose oracle has no compose mode at all — roughly 40% of the graded surface was physically absent, so the v2 verifier's 0.0 measures image drift on a mutable docker tag, not the agent.

r01 was handed a stale 12-test skeleton from the mutable docker tag while the mounted verifier greps /app/src/lib.rs for 14 test-name literals, so a genuinely correct Gear-CDC implementation that passed every test present in its container scored 0.0.

r01's container was seeded with a different, broken /app/polyhedra.py (no canary header, conway_truncate missing its whole vertex-cap face family, dual non-manifold, hull triangulation never dissolved), so a correct primitive k/j/e implementation scored 0.0 on ~74 regression checks of pre-existing code the instruction never asks about — while the instruction's one load-bearing constraint ("primitive, not composed") is verified nowhere.

At least five rollouts left container states that pass all 22 tests under the exact cryptography version test.sh pins (42.0.5) yet scored 0.0 — the graded outcome matches the image's older cryptography 41.0.7, where PSS.MAX_LENGTH verification is an exact-salt check that rejects the standard TUF salt_length=32 signatures every solver produced.

In 1 of 14 containers the task file shipped truncated — /app/algorithms.py and /opt/task_data/algorithms.py were both a 6-function, 2888-byte file missing count_inversions and max_subarray_sum (canonical is 3914 bytes, 8 functions) — making the graded task unreachable for r01, which did everything achievable and still scored 0.

The task ships from a mutable docker tag with replay_dockerfile=false, and r01's container (2026-06-14) served the unmodified NVIDIA-sample kernels with no ANISO_Z/Y/X, no DIVIDEND and no WINDOW defines, making the constants the verifier hardcodes literally unrecoverable — r01 implemented exactly what its source specified and was scored 0.

The pinned docker image ships a completely different input dataset (a 2009 ISDA CDS book) than the instruction and tests describe, so four assertions KeyError on the market_data fixture no matter what any solver writes — I verified the task is unpassable at 45/49 max, while a fabricated constants-only results.json scores 49/49 when the correct market data is present.

The mutable docker tag served two different environments across the retained set: r01 (2026-06-14) got a truncated 2378-byte safety_spec.json missing the airworthiness, required_actions and fleet-recommendation rules the instruction promises, making its 0.0 unattainable-by-construction, while all 13 runs from 2026-06-21 onward got the fixed 7451-byte spec and passed.

r01 alone was given a stale image build whose /app/README.md (1344 bytes) omits the three anomaly-scoring keys the verifier hardcodes, while the instruction delegates the output schema entirely to that README — correct work scored 0.0 purely because of which container the run drew.

The single failing run (r01) was graded against a rekey() API that did not exist anywhere in its container: it ran an older build of the mutable docker tag (sketch.py 3290 B, no rekey stub, SPEC.md with no Re-keying section, pipeline.py with one alpha and no rekey call) while the verifier's six TestRekey tests call sketch.rekey(alpha) — an unpinned-image false negative on otherwise complete, correct work.

r01's container shipped an older /app/schema/output_schema.json that names max_relative_error as the Pareto dimension while the verifier dominates on p99_max_relative_error, so a rollout that followed the instruction's explicitly delegated spec exactly was scored 0.0; separately, the suite never checks the pipeline fix or the benchmark numbers against ground truth.

Grading logic is sound and demanding, but r01 ran in a stale container image missing the block_sync stub, spec Section 7, and the testbench's entire Part C — making Part 2's required port interface unobtainable and its 0.0 an environment-caused false negative.

One of 14 containers was provisioned with a 20-patient dataset instead of 24, and because test_state.py:91-94 hardcodes `patients_tested == 24 and patients_passing == 24`, the one rollout that did complete, honest work (r01) could only have passed by reporting a count that was false in its own container.

TASK.md falsely claims the DuckDB sqlite extension is "pre-installed" (it is absent from the image), so all 10 rollouts wrote bare `LOAD sqlite`; the 5 that scored 0 produced numerically identical CSVs to the 5 that scored 1.0 and differ only by lacking the `INSTALL sqlite` line the instruction told them was unnecessary.

The verifier hardcodes base_rtt_ms = 1/20/40 ms, exactly half the RTT the shipped captures exhibit (min ack_rtt = 2.006/40.008/80.353 ms) and half the generator's own constants — the pcaps handed to 13 of 14 rollouts contain no TCP handshake at all, so the demanded value is unobtainable by any measurement and even the packet's own reference solution now fails.

The grading contract itself is sound and passable (reference scores 54/56 here, failing only on locally-absent tshark; two rollouts passed cleanly from the spec alone), but rollout r01 ran against a stale container image whose `/app/derp_protocol_spec.md` (4206 B) and `/app/output_schema.json` (8332 B) omit every section the verifier grades, making that run unwinnable, and `/tests/test_state.py` is readable in-container during the agent phase (r11 read all 1775 lines before writing code).

r01 was served a stale container image missing /app/run_benchmark.py — the only place the verifier's unstated JSON schema ("1e-04"/accepted_steps/i_controller) is discoverable — so it did all five bug fixes and both controllers correctly and still scored 0.0.

The verifier's session fixture downloads the DuckDB tpch extension over the network at grade time (test_state.py:31 `INSTALL tpch`), which fails in a minority of containers and zeroes correct solutions — r14 proved its code passes all 8 graded comparisons via `LOAD tpch` yet scored 0.0, while r13, hit by the identical failure, edited the graded /tests/test_state.py to swallow the INSTALL and scored 1.0.

Concurrently-running rollouts of this task share 127.0.0.1:5300/5353 — one container's dig is answered by another container's named/unbound — and both zeros (r13, r15) are runs whose verifier window coincided with a sibling rollout's broken DNS state, despite complete and demonstrably working on-disk artifacts.

The mutable image tag served two different Ramulator codebases mid-sweep: r13-r16 got a restructured fork in which 7 of 8 frozen assertions (and the reference solve.sh itself) are unsatisfiable by honest work, so four correct solves scored 0.0 — while the verifier is simultaneously so weak that a stub would have scored 1.0.

The container image silently drifted from Ramulator 2.0 to Ramulator 2.1 for the Jun-28 rollout batch, and the verifier plus the reference solution are hardwired to 2.0 — so r13/r14/r15/r16 did real, honest work against the code actually shipped and were all zeroed, while the task's own gold solve.sh would also score 0.0 in that image.

The verifier force-downgrades to mlflow==2.14.3 after the agent works, and mlflow 2.14.3 cannot read a file store written by today's mlflow 3.x (run meta.yaml has run_id but no run_uuid), so all 15 rollouts scored 0.0 despite producing fully spec-compliant reports and MLflow runs.

The verifier reads the DEM through the image's numpy-1.x-ABI osgeo GDAL bindings, so the one legal setup step the task itself nudges toward (`pip install rasterio`, which now hard-requires numpy>=2) silently destroys the grader — 12 rollouts whose artifacts are numerically identical to the two passing runs all scored 0.

Container-image drift: r01 ran against an /app/pipeline.py that lacked the `annotate_secondary_structure` placeholder entirely, so the verifier's required SS schema (key "ss", labels H/E/C, min run 4/2 chain-aware) was undiscoverable in its container — the sole pass/fail discriminator across all 11 rollouts is which image version was mounted, not work quality.

The task ships a mutable, unpinned docker tag and r01 was executed against an older variant of the image whose /app/spec.md and draft overlay lack the pinctrl, thermal-zone, can-5v0, idle-state, reset-gpios and startup-delay-us requirements that the packet's verifier grades, so a complete, self-verified solution scored 0.0 through no fault of the solver.

The grader is substantive and 13/15 rewards are right, but it launches its own server on the same fixed ports in the same container without checking it won the bind, so r10's verifiably 24/24-correct server.py scored 0.0 purely because an orphaned debug process split-brained UDP 2053 from TCP 8080.

test.sh's `cd /app` is a no-op under the `pytest` console script, so the scaffold's own module-level `from annotators import ...` raises at collection (exit 2) and zeroed 14 of 15 rollouts that had correctly fixed every seeded defect.

The single failing rollout (r01) was served a stale, pre-rewrite /app/flow_metrics.tcl (605 lines, header advertises "comparison") that contains no routing-convergence or timing-budget sections at all, while the verifier demands those two artifacts with exact tcl-only key names — the other 14 rollouts got the rewritten 701-line spec and passed, so the reward turned on an environment version skew, not on solver quality.

r01's container shipped a stale protocol_spec.yaml with no sensitivity_analysis section at all, so its otherwise field-for-field-correct artifact was zeroed for omitting a section its only source of truth never mentioned; separately, the verifier's tolerances are internally contradictory (it blesses a 1-patient partition difference at below_n ±5 / cohort-B ±3 while failing the chi-squared and required_n that difference necessarily produces), which zeroed r06 on 2 of 54 assertions.

r01 was served a stale pre-mutation container image whose spec.md and skeleton (standard Karras, `rho=7`, no `alpha` kwarg) contradicted both the instruction and the v2 verifier, making its 0.0 unwinnable; separately, 3 of the 6 headline deliverables are never asserted, a latent false-positive surface no retained rollout exploited.

r01 ran against a drifted image whose /app/data/ was missing report_schema.json — the file the instruction names as the sole definition of the report's fields — making four verifier-required report keys unknowable and scoring correct raster work 0.0.

The container image drifted between rollouts: r01 (2026-06-14) received a 123-line /app/visa_contactless.spthy with no LEMMAS TODO block, so the six lemma names the verifier hard-codes were undiscoverable, and its otherwise-correct Tamarin work scored 0.0; the ten later rollouts got a 136-line file that lists those exact names.

tests/test_state.py:367 calls `v.dtype.kind` on every NetCDF variable, which raises AttributeError for NetCDF4 vlen string variables (dtype is the Python `str` class) — a legal, canonical idiom used by the task's own reference solution — so four rollouts with fully compliant artifacts were errored to 0.0, in an os.listdir-order-dependent way.

All three zeros are non-substantive: r08's fully correct solution is failed only by the undocumented `len(processors) >= 4` gate (it used 3 processors doing identical work), r01's container shipped a /app/spec.md missing the entire Risk Classification section the verifier hardcodes, and r10 lost a localhost:9200 race against sibling containers that were visibly deleting each other's index.

The grading contract is strict and correct and 13/14 passes are fully earned, but r01 was provisioned with the wrong container image — /app/l2.ungrammar (the file the instruction names as "the full grammar specification") was absent and /app/src/lib.rs was the pre-v1 parser — and it failed on exactly the two conventions that missing file uniquely encodes.

Concurrent rollouts of this task share localhost:8080 but not filesystems, so a rollout that loses the port race has its POST persisted into a neighbour's container and scores 0 for flawless work — r15 is exactly that, and the same collision hit r04 and r09.

The container was not identical across rollouts: r01 (the only failure, and the earliest run) was served an /app/audit_schema.json that omits the entire data_validation sub-schema whose ~15 exact key names the verifier hard-requires, so its otherwise fully correct audit scored 0.0.

The verifier's "independent" cachegrind run omits --cache-sim=yes, and the container ships valgrind 3.22 where that option defaults to no, so the expected d_refs/d1_misses/lld_misses are all 0 — every honestly measured value is graded wrong, zeroing 11 otherwise-complete rollouts.

r01's container shipped a 14-line-shorter /app/edm.py missing the sample_dpmpp_2s and estimate_convergence_order(sampler_name, base_steps=20, batch_size=2) stubs that all 14 passing rollouts read at line 251 — making the verifier's mandatory calling convention unlearnable in that one environment, so substantively correct work scored 0.0.

Concurrent rollouts of this instance share PID and network namespaces while the spec forces every one of them onto the same fixed loopback ports and the same process name `etcd`, so a sibling's port grab or `pkill etcd` (the exact command the reference solution itself runs) destroys another rollout's live etcd before its verifier runs — three rollouts with demonstrably correct, self-verified PKI and mTLS scored 0.

Concurrent rollouts of this task share PID and network namespaces (separate filesystems only), so each rollout's routine `pkill etcd` plus rebinding of 127.0.0.1:2379 destroys a sibling's already-finished, correct solution — all three zeros (r12, r15, r16) are confirmed cross-rollout kills, not solver errors.

The task pins an unpinned mutable docker tag (replay_dockerfile=false), and r01 was handed a stale v1 image whose /app exposed only 10 zset_* functions — no zset_clone, no zset_foreach, no #[derive(Clone)] — so the v2 verifier's ctypes fixture could never bind its symbols and no possible solution in that container could score above 0.0.

The image ships a cold ~/.m2 and the compile gate needs live Maven Central, but 4/15 containers had total network blackout — two runs (r13, r16) did complete, correct migrations and scored 0 solely because `mvn compile` could not fetch the Spring Boot parent POM, while the verifier source was also readable inside the container at /workspace/_copy_dirs/tests/test_state.py.

All four zero-reward rollouts did the cryptography exactly right and were punished by environment defects: three died because the agent image ships no `cryptography` at all (so they self-verified under 48/49 where `copy.deepcopy` of an X25519 key works) while tests/test.sh pins `cryptography==44.0.3` where the identical PoC raises TypeError, and the fourth ran against a stale docker tag whose /app was `NotImplementedError` stubs with no import candidates.

The image ships without the "pre-installed" Rust nightly+Miri the instruction promises, so reward is decided entirely by whether the solver happened to type `--default-toolchain nightly` while repairing the container: all 5 that did scored 1.0, all 10 that installed stable-as-default and verified with the equally valid `cargo +nightly miri test` scored 0.0 despite producing deliverables identical in substance to the reference solution.

The single zero (r01) ran against a stale build of the mutable docker tag whose crate contained no `ProcessResult` alias, no `mod sealed`/`Codec` trait and no `Send + Sync` on `Pipeline`, making 5 of the 20 verifier tests unsatisfiable no matter what the agent did — while the 14 passes are all genuine, earned against the newer image.

The task image ships an empty ~/.m2, so both the solve and the verifier's own rebuild hard-depend on live Maven Central egress — and in 4 of 15 containers every Maven repo host was blackholed, scoring 0.0 for four rollouts (r13, r14, r15, r16) whose /app source state was the reference solution, a failure the oracle solve.sh would share.

r01's container shipped a reduced 5-defect build of the pipeline, so its complete, verified fix plus a truthful 5-entry audit was zeroed by test_state.py:204's unstated `len(data) >= 6` gate — a bar unsatisfiable in that container without inventing a sixth bug.

Concurrent rollouts share TCP port 9876 and the process table, so only one container's server can bind: at least four rollouts (r06, r07, r08, r09) performed the intended RSA forgery perfectly but were served by ANOTHER rollout's server, making their own /app/.flag_hash — the grader's "expected" value — impossible to match.

The graded scores for ".vimrc"/"/.vimrc" were transcribed from fzf *master* (bonusFor `class >= charNonWord`), but the container ships an older fzf whose bonusFor is `class > charNonWord`, so a port that provably matches the source the task tells you to reverse-engineer fails exactly 4 of 112 all-or-nothing assertions and scores 0.

tests/test.sh rotates the AES key and deletes /app/challenge.json, then re-runs only the oracle-solution path /solution/solve.sh — a path the instruction never mentions and that does not exist in agent mode — so the stated deliverable (/app/answer.json) is stale by construction and all 15 cryptographically correct rollouts scored 0.0.

The grader runs in the agent's own container and needs GDAL 3.8.4's numpy-1.x-only osgeo bindings, so any `pip install` of the (deliberately absent) geopandas/rasterio stack pulls numpy 2.x and zeroes runs whose three output artifacts are numerically identical to the passing ones — 10 of 15 rollouts died on this hidden coupling, while the assertions themselves are shallow enough that a fabricated raster would score 1.0.

The pass/fail split is exactly "did the agent leave numpy 2.x installed" — pip-installing geopandas/rasterio (sanctioned: allow_internet=true, and the image ships neither) force-upgrades the Debian numpy 1.26.4 that the verifier's own `osgeo.gdal_array` C extension is ABI-pinned to, zeroing rollouts whose three deliverables are demonstrably perfect.

r01 was run against a stale image whose /app/spec/protocol.md omits the three field groups the verifier requires (Murphy reliability/resolution/uncertainty, significant_vs_next, ranking_agreement), so its otherwise numerically-perfect solution was unachievably scored 0; the other 13 rollouts ran on the enriched protocol and were graded correctly.

r01 ran against an older /app/output_spec.json that specified the polygon vertex order P01,P03,P05,P07,P09 and distance pairs P05_P07/P07_P09/P09_P01, the exact opposite cycle from tests/test_state.py:28-29, so obeying the spec file the instruction points to was arithmetically guaranteed to score 0.0.

The verifier recomputes its elevation ground truth with `band.ReadAsArray()` through the Debian numpy-1.26.4-built osgeo bindings inside the agent's own python3, so the ordinary `pip install rasterio/geopandas` (which forces numpy 2.x in this image) errors one test and zeroes 14 rollouts whose deliverables were all verifiably correct.

Following the instruction's "Install needed packages with pip" installs schemathesis, which drags in pytest 9.x and registers a pytest11 entry point; tests/test.sh:5 then force-downgrades to pytest==8.3.4, so at grade time the plugin import dies with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_pytest.subtests', pytest exits 1 with zero tests collected, and every rollout gets a hard 0.0 no matter how correct its work.
